correctness.rationale: Over C the row-column scaling preserves both ideals. The one-parameter weights ni+j (0-based indices) are distinct, so the invariant (k+1)-dimensional vector subspaces are exactly the coordinate ones. Restriction to any such subspace retains distinct permutation monomials with nonzero coefficients in both minors and permanents; it vanishes identically for all r-blocks precisely when there is no r-matching. Euler localization for the reduced complex algebraic space identifies its compactly supported Euler characteristic with that of the fixed locus, and the Fano schemes are projective. Thus both Euler characteristics count the same finite set without any scheme-multiplicity weights. By Konig's theorem an admissible graph has a cover with at most r-1 vertices, each of degree at most n, proving the threshold for q=k+1. For r=2, pairwise intersecting edges in a simple bipartite graph with at least two edges have a unique common center, proving the two disjoint star counts. The combinatorial checker was inspected, not run; it cannot check Euler localization and is unnecessary for the proof.
residual_risks: Only ordinary Euler characteristic of the underlying complex space is asserted; no equal Betti numbers, scheme-theoretic fixed structures, or equality of motives is inferred.
